thread:
Irene Morales: Quick update — we’ve opened a small warm/burst pool of MI250X for Dedicated in the Nairobi (NBO) region starting today. This is intended for short-lived spike capacity for customers who need lower-latency regional inference.

Devon K: Nice, any limits on burst size or duration?

Irene Morales: Yep — initial pool = 40 MI250X GPUs, per-tenant max burst = 8 GPUs, burst window = 6 hours max per reservation. Customers can request a soft extension via support but will be subject to availability. :calendar:

Samir Patel: Is this available for both Reserved Dedicated and Private?

Irene Morales: Only for Dedicated warm pools (hosted Dedicated tenants). Private/VPC deployments not affected. We’ll publish an on-prem package separately if/when partners procure MI250X hardware.

Maya Chen: What's the rollout plan and can we do a canary with a few customers first?

Irene Morales: Canary today with three customers (selected from enterprise list) for 48h to monitor utilization and any perf regressions. Full self-serve reservations will open next Tue (T+4).

Alex R: Ops ask — what alerts/runbook should oncall use if queueing spikes or preemption occurs?

Irene Morales: Ops runbook pinned below. Key checks: GPU provisioning failures, evictions, and scheduler backlog. If burst pool drops below 10% free, auto-notify infra-backfill.

OpsBot: RUNBOOK LINK: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mi250x-nbo-burst

Irene Morales: Reservation CLI examples for CS/SEs to demo to customers:

```
# reserve 4 MI250X GPUs for 3 hours
redwoodctl capacity reserve --pool mi250x-nbo-burst --count 4 --duration 3h --team acme-corp
```

Irene Morales: Pricing note: burst rate = Dedicated on-demand * 1.25 multiplier (covers cross-region buffer & premium scheduling). This is temporary while warm pool is small. Billing shows as "burst-dedicated" line item.

Samir Patel: Any model/quantization caveats? Some models spike memory on first request.

Irene Morales: Good call — recommend using pinned smaller batch sizes on first 5k tokens while KV warms. We’re also shipping an optimized kernel build for MI250X tomorrow that should smooth cold-start memory pressure.

Devon K: Who owns the customer communication and the docs?

Irene Morales: CS owns customer outreach; docs owned by eng-docs + product. Draft doc posted here: https://redwood.internal/docs/mi250x-nbo-burst (please review).

Maya Chen: Anything special for quotas? Do we need to adjust global quota checks to allow burst reservations?

Irene Morales: Yes — quota service has been updated to include a transient "burst_quota" bucket. This bypasses some steady-state caps but still enforces per-tenant burst limits. Engineering: watch metrics quota.burst.* for anomalies.

Alex R: Ops note: schedule a 11:00 UTC health check for the next 3 days to validate scheduler behavior under regional traffic.

Irene Morales: Added. TL;DR for the channel: small MI250X warm pool live in NBO for Dedicated, per-tenant burst cap = 8, 6h max, canary today, self-serve next Tue, pricing multiplier 1.25, runbook + CLI examples linked. Ping me for access requests or edge cases. :rocket:

Samir Patel: Thanks — will loop in a couple customers and watch perf.

Devon K: Thanks team! :thumbsup:
